manuscript_claim: AETHER's 100 GtCO2/year gross target is about 2.4x current anthropogenic CO2 emissions and would give 57.8 GtCO2/year simple net removal before rebound.
evidence_anchor: Current emissions baseline is 42.2 GtCO2/year; simple net is 100 - 42.2 = 57.8 GtCO2/year.
reviewer_risk: Low for arithmetic; medium for interpreting simple net as climate outcome.
required_upgrade: Keep carbon-cycle caveat next to any ppm or net-removal statement.
paper_usage_rule: Can state as arithmetic, not as realized atmospheric drawdown.

manuscript_claim: Current CDR is orders of magnitude below AETHER scale.
evidence_anchor: State of CDR 2026 reports about 2.2 GtCO2/year total CDR and about 2.04 MtCO2/year novel CDR.
reviewer_risk: Low if wording distinguishes conventional land CDR from novel engineered CDR.
required_upgrade: Keep current CDR source refreshed before submission.

manuscript_claim: Reduced-form carbon-cycle modeling makes emissions decline and rebound control decisive.
evidence_anchor: No-AETHER constant emissions reaches 656 ppm by 2100; net-zero 2050 plus AETHER reaches the 350 ppm floor; 58% rebound remains near 473 ppm.
reviewer_risk: Medium because the Joos impulse-response screen is not a full Earth-system model.
required_upgrade: Run FAIR-class or Earth-system-model workflows with state-dependent removal response.
paper_usage_rule: Use as scenario discipline, not final climate prediction.

manuscript_claim: A 3 GJ/tCO2 AETHER system is a tens-of-terawatts clean-power problem.
evidence_anchor: 91,667 TWh/year gross clean generation, 27.5 TW nameplate, and 3.5 TW firm clean capacity in the balanced case.
reviewer_risk: Medium because dispatch, transmission, curtailment, and siting remain coarse.
required_upgrade: Regional dispatch, interconnection, transmission, and storage-duration model.
paper_usage_rule: Can state as first-order buildout screen.

manuscript_claim: Full CO2 splitting is compact but not the default AETHER storage pathway.
evidence_anchor: CO2 splitting floor is about 8.94 GJ/tCO2, adding about 248,333 TWh/year at 100 GtCO2/year before real losses.
reviewer_risk: Low for thermodynamic floor; high for any product-market interpretation.
required_upgrade: Add real electrochemical efficiency, separations, oxygen handling, and carbon product safety model.
paper_usage_rule: Can state as lower-bound energy caution.

manuscript_claim: The current 100 GtCO2/year pathway portfolio is an upper-tail stress test, not a forecast.
evidence_anchor: AETHER portfolio uses 100 GtCO2/year against 37.5 GtCO2/year central assessed potential sum and 107.6 GtCO2/year high assessed sum.
reviewer_risk: High unless each pathway gets regional cost and potential curves.
required_upgrade: Regionalized pathway distributions and substitution rules.
paper_usage_rule: Label as stress test and upper-tail dependency.

manuscript_claim: Gross capture is not durable credited removal.
evidence_anchor: 100 GtCO2/year gross portfolio credits 84.9 GtCO2/year after lifecycle and durability haircuts; 117.8 GtCO2/year gross is needed for 100 GtCO2/year durable credit at the same mix.
reviewer_risk: High because lifecycle and durability haircuts are route-level assumptions.
required_upgrade: Full pathway-specific LCA and basin-level storage model.
paper_usage_rule: Use as a cautionary filter, not final credit accounting.

manuscript_claim: Air-contactor scale is a hardware and factory-rate bottleneck.
evidence_anchor: 100 Gt all-air NASEM-reference case needs 3,771 km2 contactor face area, 9,290 TWh/year fan electricity, and 200,000 STRATOS-scale equivalents.
reviewer_risk: Medium-high because module geometry, pressure drop, fouling, and uptime are simplified.
required_upgrade: Factory-rate model for modules, sorbents, maintenance, and failure rates.

manuscript_claim: AI and robotics can move automatable buckets but do not erase delivered-tonne floors.
evidence_anchor: Current DAC-like stack is about $606/tCO2; automation push is about $86/tCO2; deep-abundance floor is about $24/tCO2.
reviewer_risk: High because cost reductions are hand-set scenario assumptions.
required_upgrade: Component-level TEA and sourced learning distributions by pathway.
paper_usage_rule: Use as plausibility frontier, not forecast.

manuscript_claim: Robot production and robot counts are not the same as useful autonomous AETHER labor.
evidence_anchor: AETHER portfolio push has robot adequacy ratio 13.7x under optimistic proxy assumptions, but field task productivity remains unproven.
reviewer_risk: High if company claims are treated as independent productivity evidence.
required_upgrade: Task-family distributions for duty cycle, reliability, supervision, maintenance, and productive output.
paper_usage_rule: Use robotics claims as leads or anchors, not proof of field productivity.

manuscript_claim: The integrated 2046 screen passes only under simultaneous favorable assumptions.
evidence_anchor: AETHER portfolio push passes, while the fast energy-constrained case reaches only 20% of target capacity.
reviewer_risk: High because several assumptions are correlated and hand-set.
required_upgrade: Correlated probabilistic scenario model with sourced distributions.

manuscript_claim: The uncertainty screen makes 100 GtCO2/year durable credit an upper-tail outcome.
evidence_anchor: 0.75% of hand-set samples reach 100 GtCO2/year gross capacity; 0.09% reach 100 GtCO2/year durable credit; median durable credit is 30.8 GtCO2/year.
reviewer_risk: High if interpreted as calibrated probability.
required_upgrade: Expert elicitation, source-backed distributions, and correlation structure.
paper_usage_rule: Call it a probability-like screen, not a forecast.

manuscript_claim: Jevons-style rebound can erase the simple net-negative benefit.
evidence_anchor: A 57.8% rebound or delayed-abatement penalty erases the 57.8 GtCO2/year simple net benefit against current emissions.
reviewer_risk: Medium because rebound is policy-mediated, not a single physical parameter.
paper_usage_rule: Use as failure condition and governance requirement.

manuscript_claim: Citizen-owned or trust-held atmospheric/ocean commons is an exploratory governance branch.
evidence_anchor: Commons ownership is framed as a sink-pricing and restriction mechanism, not as the core technical proof.
reviewer_risk: High because legal feasibility and political economy are under-modeled.
required_upgrade: Compare carbon tax, cap-and-dividend, atmospheric trust, liability, and bans under MRV failure modes.
paper_usage_rule: Keep exploratory unless governance model is strengthened.
